name: Oman Arab Bank
founded: 1984 per the bank's investor presentation timeline (OAB established after acquiring Arab Bank's branches in Oman; Arab Bank began operating in Oman in 1973). The timeline text is jumbled, so the years are matched to events in order. OAB acquired Alizz Islamic Bank in 2020 and became a public joint-stock company (SAOG) listed on MSX.
ownership_summary: Listed on the Muscat Stock Exchange (ticker OAB, from the MSX financial reports listing). At 31 Dec 2025 Arab Bank PLC (Jordan, listed in Amman) held 49.00%, Oman International Development & Investment Co. SAOG (Ominvest) 30.99%, and various parties including trusts 20.01% (2,002,743,333 shares). The June 2026 presentation shows the same 49% / 31% / 20% split. OAB is described as a subsidiary of Arab Bank PLC.

shareholders.holder: Oman International Development & Investment Company SAOG (Ominvest)

government_link: No direct state shareholder above 10% is disclosed. The controlling holder is Arab Bank PLC and the second is Ominvest, a listed investment company (S2). Any government link through Ominvest's own shareholders was not checked.
group_structure: Parent bank plus a 100% Islamic subsidiary, Alizz Islamic Bank (called 'Al Izz Islamic Bank (AIB)' in the H1 2026 statements; OAB owns 100%), which also owns Alizz Sukuk SPC for its sukuk issuance (S1 notes 1 and 13, S2 p.40). The consolidated numbers include Alizz; the parent-only figures are shown separately in the statements. Arab Bank's CEO is OAB's Deputy Chairman. On 16 Jul 2026 Bank Nizwa sent a non-binding letter of intent to acquire 100% of Alizz at 1.2x book value, and OAB's board accepted it on 23 Jul 2026 to proceed with discussions (S1 note 29). In 2017 OAB's Investment Management Group moved to Ubhar Capital (per the om-ubhar research file; not re-opened here).

subsidiaries.name: Alizz Islamic Bank (Al Izz Islamic Bank)
subsidiaries.activity: Islamic bank; 17 Islamic branches at FY2025 and 18 in the 1H 2026 presentation. Subject of a non-binding sale proposal from Bank Nizwa (July 2026). Not profiled in a separate file.

subsidiaries.name: Alizz Sukuk SPC
subsidiaries.activity: SPV issuing Alizz's perpetual Tier 1 sukuk (FSA-licensed SPV)

footprint: Oman only. 69 branches in the 1H 2026 presentation (51 conventional and 18 Islamic) and 166 ATMs; the FY2025 annual report counted 50 conventional and 17 Islamic branches. Arab Bank has 600+ branches in 29 countries (S2 p.30, S3 slides 12 and 14).
customer_segments: Retail mass, Elite (affluent), Elite Exclusive (invitation-only top tier), SME (Tumouhi programme), corporate, government and GREs, and Islamic retail and corporate through Alizz.
business_lines: Segments in the H1 2026 statements: Retail banking, Corporate banking, Treasury and Others for the conventional bank, plus Islamic Banking through Alizz (S1 note 28). Retail products are loans, overdrafts, cards and transfers. OAB has no separate asset management, brokerage or private banking entity.

capabilities.wealth_summary: OAB's affluent offer is Elite, launched in February 2016, open to customers with a deposit balance of OMR 35,000 or a monthly salary of OMR 3,500 (as published), with a dedicated RM, lounges and an Elite Infinite card. The launch release lists three pillars, including Elite Wealth Management (financial planning and investment services), but the current Elite page lists none. In August 2024 OAB added an invitation-only 'Elite Exclusive' tier with wealth management services, exclusive insurance, a metal card and a private deposit box. No private banking unit, fund range, discretionary service, brokerage or digital investing feature was found; the OAB Online app lists accounts, transfers, payments and service requests only. OAB's Investment Management Group moved to Ubhar Capital in 2017 and Ubhar became OAB's market maker and liquidity provider in May 2024 (per the om-ubhar research file). OAB holds no FSA securities licence. The July 2026 proposal for Bank Nizwa to buy Alizz Islamic Bank is the main structural event and would leave OAB without an Islamic franchise.

opportunities: OAB has no asset management, brokerage, funds shelf or investing feature in its app, yet it runs an affluent Elite segment (OMR 35,000 / 3,500) and an invitation-only Elite Exclusive tier that promises 'wealth management services' (S8, S9, S16).

The bank sold its investment management business to Ubhar Capital in 2017, so wealth products would have to be partnered or built; two OAB directors sit on Ubhar's board, which is a ready channel for a product tie-up (S2, om-ubhar).

Arab Bank (49%) has a GCC private banking presence (a Head of GCC Private Banking at Arab Bank plc sits on Ubhar's board per om-ubhar), giving a possible group-product route; not evidenced as an OAB offer (S2).
Net fee and commission income rose 18% in H1 2026 and the bank issued a USD 400m AT1 in June 2026, showing capital to invest, though no wealth spend is stated (S1, S3).
barriers: The Islamic franchise (Alizz, about 1.3bn of deposits) may leave through the proposed sale to Bank Nizwa, which would reshape the customer base and priorities (S1 note 29, S2).
Head-of-retail and wealth roles are not clearly staffed on the live page (Deputy Head Retail only), so there is no named wealth sponsor (S5).
The bank's stated focus is corporate and digital capability (Corporate Mobile Banking, SME platforms, Genacom) rather than wealth (S2).
Core banking is on Finastra per a 2017 announcement; later changes were not checked (S15).

open_items: Lead check: 'Alizz Islamic Bank merger' is not a pending OAB merger. OAB acquired Alizz in 2020 and holds 100%. What is pending is a July 2026 proposal that Bank Nizwa acquire 100% of Alizz from OAB at 1.2x book value, by merger by incorporation into Bank Nizwa; OAB's board accepted the non-binding letter of intent on 23 Jul 2026 to proceed with discussions (S1 note 29). Bank Nizwa's H1 2026 report says it is obtaining regulatory approvals to start due diligence. No definitive agreement was found by 12 Oct 2026; re-check MSX.
Lead check: Arab Bank plc stake is 49.00% (31 Dec 2025) and Ominvest 30.99%; Arab Bank's CEO is OAB's Deputy Chairman.

Merger check 2024-2026: no other merger involving OAB was found (no OAB-Ahli, OAB-Sohar or OAB-Bank Dhofar deal). The 2023 Ominvest-led bid for Ahli Bank was said to plan a merger of Ahli with OAB (search results, Gulf Business), but no completion was found (see om-ahlibank).
No head of wealth, private banking or asset management is named; no OAB wealth product page beyond Elite was found. The OAB website did not render a wealth or investment section in the pages fetched.
The date of the 1H 2026 employee, branch and ATM figures (1,434; 69; 166) is not stated on the slide.
Alizz's current CEO (Ali Al Mani, appointed Aug 2023 per search results) and its own leadership page were not opened.
Khalid Al Amri (Chief Retail Banking Officer in Aug 2024) is not on the live page or in the FY2025 report; no departure news found.
Q3 2026 results were not published on the IR page on 12 Oct 2026. Re-check late October.
